## 2026-11-16T02:05Z — fes-f2-gpu on an A100: current main is about 2.5 times shorter per call; the remaining time is not pipe latency [pcc:unverified] (Claude)


- Corrected my own timer on 13 November (the worker's "read" phase included the wait for the next request) and dropped the request-parse lead; then found `main` already carried PR #4101 (binary `--serve-bin` protocol, single-copy CUDA upload). Details of the correction are in the 2026-11-13 log.
- Host: with `--serve-bin`, a null worker (parse, answer no solutions) gives a round trip of 28 us per call; the real host worker 0.45 to 0.52 ms (walk compute included). [pcc:unverified]
- One Modal A100 80GB PCIe job (`research/ic_gpu_ipc_split_20261116/`: `job_ipc.sh`, `run_arms.sh`, `null_bin.cpp`, `modal_ipc.py`, `analyze.py`, `make_fig.py`), three interleaved arms, three runs each, koblitz n23 (24 unknowns) and char2 n25 (26 unknowns); record `20261116T0058Z-ic-gpu-ipc-split-a100` (closed, measured), report, figure and 51 raw files in the directory. Before the arms: text and binary smoke tests CUDA equals host, selftest ran. A dry run of `run_arms.sh` on the host (host worker standing in for CUDA) caught no script errors. [pcc:unverified]
- Results (mean of 3 runs per arm): whole solver call, `ic` before the direct pack with the text protocol to current `main` with the binary protocol, 0.5009 to 0.2028 ms at 24 unknowns and 0.6310 to 0.2753 ms at 26 (59.5 and 56.4 percent less); counted answers identical in 5 of 5 compared runs. On `main` at 24 unknowns: kernel 0.069 ms, worker busy 0.093 ms, round trip 0.192 ms, null-worker pipe floor 0.0135 ms, so about 0.085 ms of the round trip is in none of those phases (0.079 ms at 26 unknowns). [pcc:unverified]


- The 2026-11-13 guess that the unlocated time was pipe wake-up latency is not supported: the floor is 13.5 us in the container and 28 us on the host. The remainder is not yet identified; candidates (worker thread waking cold between requests, `cudaStreamSynchronize` yielding rather than spinning, first-launch latency after idle) are untested.
- The A to B difference is not attributed to one change: it spans PR #4062, PR #4101 and whatever else reached `main` between the two `ic` builds. Only the phase table attributes it.
- Did not edit `.resume/RESUME.md`: it is tracked and holds another session's handoff (the rho study, PR #4237). The S3 checkpoint gate was waived by the owner for this one run (answer to a question, 2026-11-16); `CHECKPOINT_SKIP` reason recorded in the launch command's environment.
- No `benchmarks/README.md` or leaderboard row: wall time only, counted cost unchanged, no validator report or matched rho (validation gate).


- A second A100 job to A/B the candidates for the 0.085 ms remainder against arm B (opt-in worker flags: spin-wait sync via `cudaSetDeviceFlags(cudaDeviceScheduleSpin)`, a short `poll()` spin before blocking on stdin). Needs another waiver or a checkpoint token, and the flag code is not written.
- The kernel is 34 percent of a call at 24 unknowns; beyond the per-call floor the lever is batching several systems per launch (#4101's timers were added for that bound).
- `docs/session-logs/2026-11-15.md` on `main` contains 10 unresolved merge-conflict marker lines from other sessions; I left it as it is.


- The launching Modal client was stopped at its background time limit before the job finished, so `benchrec run` never wrote its entry and `benchrec close` refused. The job ran to completion on Modal; I fetched it by token (twice; the second fetch reproduced the archived raw file byte for byte) and recorded the fetch command under `benchrec run`, saying so in the record's summary.
- The 2026-11-15 session-log conflicted on rebase because other sessions append to it; I kept `main`'s version of that file and wrote this entry in the 2026-11-16 file instead.
